Naval bases at Berehaven, Cobh and Lough Swilly returned by Britain to Éire in 1938, denying the Royal Navy Atlantic bases once war began.
Luftwaffe raids on Belfast in April and May 1941 killed around a thousand people; the city was poorly defended and Dublin sent fire engines to help.
Harland & Wolff built ships, Short Brothers built aircraft, and farms supplied food, making Northern Ireland strategically valuable to Britain.
Ports and airfields, especially around Derry/Londonderry, protected Atlantic convoys; American troops began arriving in Northern Ireland in 1942.

mcqs.q: When did the Luftwaffe heavily bomb Belfast?
options: April and May 1941
September 1939
June 1944
May 1945

mcqs.q: Why was Northern Ireland strategically important in the Battle of the Atlantic?
options: Its ports and airfields helped protect convoys, especially after the Treaty Ports were returned to Éire in 1938
It was the only part of the UK with an army
German U-boats were based there
It supplied all of Britain's coal

mcqs.q: Was conscription introduced in Northern Ireland during the war?
options: No — it was never extended there, partly because of expected nationalist opposition
Yes — from September 1939, as in the rest of the UK
Yes — but only for women
No — because Northern Ireland was neutral

mcqs.q: Did Irish neutrality mean Éire favoured Germany?
options: Éire was officially neutral but leaned towards the Allies in practice — sharing weather reports, quietly returning Allied airmen and allowing the Donegal air corridor.
De Valera's neutrality meant Ireland secretly supported the Nazis.
Northern Ireland was occupied by Germany for most of the war.
Éire declared war on Germany in 1944.

mcqs.q: Why was Belfast so badly hit in the 1941 Blitz?
options: Belfast escaped serious bombing because it was too far from Germany.
Belfast was poorly prepared — few anti-aircraft guns, few shelters and little evacuation — because it was wrongly assumed to be beyond effective German bomber range.
Belfast was never bombed during the Second World War.
Éire declared war on Germany in 1944.

mcqs.q: Did Northern Ireland matter to the Allied war effort?
options: Northern Ireland was occupied by Germany for most of the war.
Yes — its shipyards, aircraft factories, food exports and Atlantic bases, plus the arrival of US troops from 1942, made it strategically significant.
Belfast was never bombed during the Second World War.
Northern Ireland sat out the war and contributed little because conscription was never applied there.
